missing_evidence: PO-1005 (purchase order referenced by both INV-1005 and REC-1005 but not supplied in the case file)
notes: All four supplied documents (invoice, receipt, bank statement, ledger entry) agree on vendor (GreenRoute Logistics Pvt. Ltd.), currency (INR), and total amount (59,000), and the bank/ledger entries both cite INV-1005 consistently. However, both INV-1005 and REC-1005 explicitly reference PO-1005, which is never provided, so the purchase order cannot be confirmed to exist or match terms - this is treated as missing supporting evidence rather than inferred as PO-exempt, since the documents themselves point to a PO. Additionally, REC-1005 is dated 2026-07-18, three days before the invoice date of 2026-07-21, an illogical sequence (a receipt predating the invoice it purports to satisfy) that cannot be resolved with the documents on hand and further weakens confidence. The presence of a receipt document does establish that a receipt exists, but its date anomaly means it cannot be relied upon to confirm timely fulfillment of any payment-terms condition tied to invoice issuance. The successful bank settlement (BNK-1005) confirms payment occurred but is not itself proof that any receipt-based condition was met at the correct point in the sequence. Tax amount (9,000 INR, 18% GST) is only explicitly stated on the invoice; its absence on the bank statement, ledger, and receipt is expected and not treated as a gap, since only the invoice is required to break out tax separately.
